newsitem.title: USA: Manufacturing index rises in December; markets skid.
newsitem.headline: Manufacturing index rises in December; markets skid.

text.p: A widely watched index of manufacturing activity rose in December, the nation's purchasing managers said Thursday, sending a shiver through financial markets and driving stock and bond prices lower.

The National Association of Purchasing Management said its index of maufacturing activity rose to 54.0 in December from 52.7 in November. A reading above 50 points to growth in manufacturing, while one below that level indicates contraction.
Stock and bond prices fell after the report, which apparently worried some investors that stronger economic growth might lead to a pickup in inflation and higher interest rates.

Bonds, which had risen earlier in the session, reversed course after the report, which in turn helped send the Dow Jones industrial average down about 93 points to 6,355 in early trading. The stock market was especially nervous following Tuesday's 101-point slide.
Traders in the inflation-sensitive bond market drove the 30-year Treasury bond down 1-7/32, or $12.1875 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.74 percent from 6.64 percent on Tuesday.
Bond prices and yields move in the opposite direction.
Inflation is a bond investor's worst enemy because it erodes the returns on long-term investments. The nation's financial markets were closed on Wednesday for New Year's Day.
